Subject: Unexpected latency + 429s on reserved plan since 12/30

Jonas —

We started seeing a sharp jump in median token latency and a stream of 429s hitting our reserved endpoints late last night (around 23:40 UTC on 12/30). This is on our production cluster using the reserved capacity we purchased (commit ID DEAL-8472). The app experiences timeouts for short bursts but it's now sustained and affecting user flows.

Attached are the logs the SRE team pulled (trace ids and sample requests). Key asks:
- Can you confirm whether this is a tenant isolation issue or cross-tenant scheduling?
- What mitigation can we expect in the next 2 hours? We are seeing business impact and leadership is asking for an update.

Thanks,
Emily Rogers

ClearBridge Financial

Emily — thanks for the rapid heads-up and for the logs. I'm pulling ops in now.

Quick summary for transparency:
- I see an increase in queue depth for your reserved pool and a correlated drop in throughput; we suspect spillover from an intensive hosted-API workload on the same GPU hosts (cross-tenant resource contention).
- I have looped in Marissa (SE) for customer-facing triage and Vivek (SRE/infra) for immediate investigation. Aditya — can you join the exec bridge if we need credits/contract remediation?

I'll update in 15m with initial findings.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 31 Dec 2026 17:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency + 429s on reserved plan since 12/30

Emily / team — thanks, and sorry for the trouble. I ran the log samples and can confirm: the 429s are quota throttle responses emitted by our scheduler when the reserved pool's token-throughput window was exceeded repeatedly. Two immediate items:

1) Short mitigation (minutes): we can temporarily expand your reserved QPS to a nearby compatible capacity tier within the same region (best-effort, will impact other hosted capacity). This will reduce 429s but may not fully eliminate latency from queueing.

2) Root cause hypothesis: an unexpected high-priority hosted-API batch job began ramping yesterday on hosts sharing the same GPU hardware family; kernel scheduling and memory headroom pressure allowed cross-tenant interference. Vivek — please confirm kernel preemption logs and whether the CPU offload/continuous-batching heuristics mis-assigned tokens to shared queues.

Can we start a 30-min bridge? Emily, when's earliest for you?

Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

On Thu, 31 Dec 2026 at 17:12 Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Emily / team — thanks, and sorry for the trouble. I ran the log samples and can confirm: the 429s are quota throttle responses emitted by our scheduler when the reserved pool's token-throughput window was exceeded repeatedly.

Quick infra readout (initial):
- We are seeing transient host-level saturation on 4 GPU nodes that are part of the reserved pool mapping for ClearBridge. The scheduler attempted graceful degradation (throttles) but queue growth caused latency spikes.
- Kernel selection skew and a new hosted-API micro-batch rollout (deployed 12/30 02:00 UTC) increased per-token CPU overhead; combined with a heavier-than-expected sequence length profile, the sustained load exceeded the reserved throughput envelope.

Immediate operational actions (I can run these now):
- Force-migrate problematic hosted-API slices off the impacted hosts (expected ~6–9m to enact and stabilize).
- Temporarily allocate two GPUs from general pool as emergency headroom to preserve your SLA while we fix placement rules.
- Collect and share diagnostics snapshot (will attach redwood_diagnostics_snapshot_20261231.txt).

If you approve the emergency headroom allocation, I'll start migration immediately. Otherwise we'll throttle further to keep other tenants safe.

— Vivek Kulkarni
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
